chapter.title: What Is the Scanner?
chapter.subtitle: Why automated screening beats gut feeling

slides.title: The Problem with Manual Trading
slides.text: Most retail traders lose money because of three human flaws: emotion, inconsistency, and analysis paralysis. You see a stock pumping, you chase it. It drops, you panic-sell. Or worse — you spend hours analyzing and never pull the trigger. The scanner solves all three by removing YOU from the equation.

slides.title: What the Scanner Does Every Day
items: Scans 116 tickers across US, Europe, and Asia-Pacific markets
Detects the current market regime (Risk-On, Neutral, Risk-Off…)
Runs 3 screening strategies adapted to the regime
Scores each setup from 0 to 100 on 4 factors
Selects the Top 10 A+ setups with entry, stop-loss, and targets
Publishes everything: website, Telegram, YouTube — fully automated

slides.question: Why can a 50% win rate still be highly profitable?
choices: It can't — you need at least 60% to make money
Because average wins are larger than average losses (asymmetric R/R)
Because losing trades are free
Because the broker refunds your losses
slides.explanation: With average wins of +10.3% and average losses of -6.95%, even a 50/50 hit rate produces a 1.7× profit factor. It's the SIZE of wins vs losses that matters, not the frequency.

slides.title: Safety Filters: What Gets REJECTED
slides.text: Before any ticker makes the Top 10, it passes through two critical filters. First: the Anti-Dilution filter checks SEC filings for shelf registrations, warrants, ATM offerings, and toxic fund involvement. Second: the Anti-Duplicate filter ensures no ticker appears twice in the portfolio simultaneously. A perfect score of 99 gets rejected if the ticker is already in your open positions.

slides.question: A stock scores 96 but has an active ATM offering (At-The-Market dilution program). What happens?
choices: It makes the Top 10 because the score is excellent
It gets a warning label but stays in
It is immediately REJECTED regardless of score
It goes into a special high-risk category
slides.explanation: Dilution risk overrides everything. An ATM offering means the company can sell new shares at any time, crashing the price. No score can compensate for that structural risk. This filter was added after the INDO incident — a perfect technical setup that got crushed by dilution.

chapter.title: The 5 Portfolio Modes
chapter.subtitle: Same signals, five risk profiles — pick yours

slides.title: One Scanner, Five Portfolios
slides.text: The scanner generates the same 10 signals every day. But HOW you use them depends on your risk tolerance. We run 5 model portfolios simultaneously — Turbo, Dynamic, Balanced, Secured, and Fortress — each with different position sizing, rotation rules, and risk limits. Same signals, completely different outcomes.

slides.title: Turbo Mode — Maximum Firepower
slides.text: Turbo mode puts 100% into a single position using momentum and breakout setups. It locks in breakeven at just +0.5% gain, trails daily at 2%, and sells half at TP1 while trailing the rest. Win rate is only 50%, but the average winner is 21 times the average loser — PF of 21x. Backtest: +52.47% return. For expert momentum traders only.

slides.title: Balanced Mode — The Sweet Spot
slides.text: Balanced mode holds 2 positions at 50% each. It optimizes for the best risk-adjusted returns — Sharpe and Calmar ratios. Backtest: +26.1% return with only -2.61% max drawdown. This is what we recommend for most traders. It uses daily rotation (max 1 per day) to keep the portfolio fresh.

slides.title: Fortress Mode — Sleep at Night
slides.text: Fortress mode uses the same parameters as Secured (3 slots, breakout only, 10-day horizon) but with half-sized positions — only 17% per trade instead of 33%. This mechanically halves the drawdown from -2.2% to -1.11%. Backtest: +9.29% return. Lower returns, but the max pain is just 1.1%. Designed for capital that absolutely cannot afford to lose.

slides.title: How Were These Modes Found?
slides.text: We tested 13 million parameter combinations using walk-forward validation. Twelve dimensions: portfolio size, signals count, minimum score, horizon, strategy filter, rotation, partial take-profit, trailing stop, max stop %, ATR multiplier, daily trail %, breakeven %, stale days, and position sizing. The optimizer identified 5 configurations across 40 live scans — from extreme alpha (Turbo) to ultra-safe capital preservation (Fortress).

slides.question: You have $10,000 and choose Balanced mode (2 slots at 50%). How much goes into each position?
slides.explanation: $10,000 divided by 4 positions equals $2,500 per slot. That's your position size. If the stop loss is 6% below entry, your maximum risk per trade is $2,500 times 6% equals $150 — just 1.5% of your total portfolio.

When a Signal Times Out
slides.text: If price hasn't hit TP1 or the stop loss by the end of the horizon window — typically 5 or 10 days — you close at market price, whatever it is. This is NOT a failure. CRM expired at plus 4.94% after 5 days — a decent profit even though it didn't reach the target. Timeouts prevent you from holding dead positions forever.

slides.question: XLE is currently at $62.56 with TP1 at $63.00 (only 0.7% away) and 4 days left. What should you do?
choices: Sell now and lock in the +11.2% gain
Wait — it's 96% of the way to TP1, let the system work
Buy more to average up

slides.explanation: The system is mechanical for a reason. XLE is 96% of the way to TP1 with 4 days remaining. Let it play out. If it hits TP1, you sell half and trail the rest. If it times out, you still exit with a solid +11% gain. Don't outsmart the system.

chapter.title: Position Sizing & Risk
chapter.subtitle: What '25% allocation' really means — with math

steps.title: Know Your Mode
steps.description: Calmar = 4 slots. Your allocation per position is 100% ÷ 4 = 25% of total capital

steps.title: Calculate Dollar Size
steps.description: If your portfolio is $10,000, each position is $2,500. With $50,000, it's $12,500

steps.title: Calculate True Risk
steps.description: Entry $39.00, Stop $35.00 = 10.3% risk. On a 25% position: 10.3% × 25% = 2.57% portfolio risk

steps.title: Check Your Comfort
steps.description: If 2.57% portfolio risk per trade feels too high, choose Conservative mode (5% positions = 0.5% risk)

slides.title: Risk Per Trade by Mode ($10,000 Portfolio)
What Happens After Prices Move?
slides.text: You bought XLE at $56.25 with a 25% allocation. Now it's at $62.56 — up 11.2%. Your XLE position is now worth MORE than 25% of your portfolio because it grew. Do NOT rebalance mid-trade. The system tracks actual dollars, not percentages. When XLE closes (TP1, stop, or timeout), the freed capital goes back to the cash pool for the next signal. Only rebalance when opening NEW positions.

slides.title: The TP1 Split: Sell Half, Trail the Rest
slides.text: When price hits Target 1, you sell exactly 50% of your position. That locks in profits. The remaining 50% stays open with the stop loss moved to your entry price — breakeven. This way, even if the stock reverses completely, you keep your TP1 profit and lose nothing on the trailing half. If it keeps running to TP2, you double your gain.

slides.title: Maximum Drawdown Explained
slides.text: Drawdown is the biggest peak-to-valley drop in your portfolio value. Our Calmar mode has a max drawdown of minus 1.63% over 35 days. That means the worst pain you'd have felt was seeing your $10,000 portfolio drop to $9,837 before recovering. Compare that to the S and P 500 which dropped 4.2% in the same period. The scanner's worst day is a normal Tuesday for the market.

slides.question: You use Calmar mode with a $20,000 portfolio. BTU signal: entry $39, stop $35. How much money are you risking on this trade?
choices: $800 (4% of portfolio)
$5,000 (25% of portfolio)
$512 (2.56% of portfolio)
$200 (1% of portfolio)
slides.explanation: Position size = 25% of $20,000 = $5,000. Stop distance = ($39 − $35) / $39 = 10.26%. Dollar risk = $5,000 × 10.26% = $513. That's 2.56% of your total portfolio at risk on this one trade.

chapter.title: Market Regime
chapter.subtitle: How the scanner adapts to bull, bear, and everything between

slides.title: Why Regime Matters
slides.text: Running a momentum strategy in a Risk-Off market is like surfing in a hurricane. The scanner automatically shifts its strategy weights based on the detected regime. Right now, in Early Risk-Off, it favors breakout plays in energy and defensives — sectors that thrive when fear rises. It would NOT push you into high-beta tech names. The regime is the compass; the strategy is the map.

slides.title: Reading the Regime Badge
slides.text: Every scanner page and every status update shows the current regime badge at the top. Green means go aggressive with momentum. Orange means be selective, favor pullbacks in quality names. Red means maximum caution, only the strongest setups. If you see purple Recovery, it means the bottom is likely in — load up on breakouts. Always check the regime before placing orders.

slides.question: The VIX spikes to 32 and markets drop 3% in a day. What does the scanner do?
choices: Stops generating signals — too dangerous
Switches to Risk-Off: favors pullback plays in defensive sectors
Goes all-in on momentum tech stocks
Shorts the market
slides.explanation: The scanner never stops. In Risk-Off (VIX 25-35), it shifts to Pullback strategies (50%) in defensive sectors like energy, utilities, and gold. It looks for oversold quality names that bounced off support. The scanner adapts — it doesn't hide.

slides.title: Convergence = Your Returns Match the Model
slides.text: After about 10 trading days — roughly 2 calendar weeks — your actual portfolio will hold the same positions as the model. From that point forward, your returns should closely track what the status page shows. The first 10 days might differ because you're building up from zero while the model already had positions. Be patient during the ramp-up.

slides.title: Common Mistakes When Starting
slides.text: Number one: don't cherry-pick signals. If you only buy the ones you 'like', you're adding your bias back in — defeating the whole purpose. Number two: don't skip the stop loss. Ever. One runaway loss can wipe out weeks of gains. Number three: don't change modes mid-week. Commit to one mode for at least a full cycle, then evaluate. The system needs time to prove itself.

slides.question: You started following Calmar mode 3 days ago. Your returns are −0.5% while the model shows +2.1%. Should you worry?
choices: Yes — the system is broken, switch to a different mode
No — you haven't converged yet, give it 7 more trading days
Yes — sell everything and wait for a better entry
No — but you should double your position sizes to catch up
slides.explanation: You're only 3 days in — convergence takes about 10 trading days for Calmar. The model had existing positions earning returns before you started. Once your portfolio fully cycles through, your returns will track the model. Patience is the edge.

slides.title: Telegram Alerts — Never Miss a Signal
slides.text: Every evening after the scan runs, you get a Telegram message with everything you need. New BUY orders for vacant slots, positions that need action — like an expiring position or one near its stop — the full top 10 signals with scores, and a portfolio risk visualization. One glance and you know exactly what to do tomorrow morning. No chart-staring required.

items: 📊 Performance snapshot: daily return, drawdown, win rate, profit factor
📥 New BUY orders: ticker, entry, stop, TP1, TP2, R/R, allocation %
⛔ Action required: positions that expired, hit stops, or need closing
📂 Open positions: current P&L, days remaining for each
⚖️ Portfolio risk bar: visual worst-case to best-case range
📡 Full Top 10 signals with scores and strategies

slides.title: YouTube Recaps & Retrospectives
slides.text: Every week, we publish a video retrospective on YouTube. It covers all the scans from the past 10 days: which signals hit their targets, which got stopped, and the overall hit rate. The retrospective assigns a grade from A-plus to F based on two pillars — setup hit rate and portfolio simulation performance. It's your weekly report card for the system.

slides.title: The Daily Card — Your Morning Cheat Sheet
slides.text: Every day, a visual daily card image is generated and posted to Telegram. It shows the top 3 signals with Finviz charts, the current regime badge, portfolio status, and action items — all in one image you can check in 10 seconds on your phone. Pin it, screenshot it, share it. It's designed to be your one-glance morning briefing.

slides.title: The Golden Rule
slides.text: Trust the system. Don't override it with your feelings. The scanner exists precisely because human judgment fails under pressure. Place the orders, respect the stops, take the exits. In 35 days of live tracking, a 50% win rate with asymmetric risk-reward produced plus 5.46% return with only minus 1.63% drawdown. The math works. Let it work for you.

slides.question: Final question: What is the single most important discipline for following the scanner successfully?
choices: Picking only the highest-scoring signals
Using the Growth mode for maximum returns
Following EVERY signal mechanically without emotional override
Checking prices every 5 minutes
slides.explanation: The scanner's edge comes from consistency. If you cherry-pick, skip stops, or override exits, you're adding human bias — the exact thing the system removes. Follow every signal, respect every stop, take every exit. The math does the rest. Welcome to systematic trading.
